category: Semiconductor lithography equipment — extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and deep ultraviolet (DUV) systems used to print circuitry onto silicon wafers for chip fabrication.
price: Not price-competitive by design — each EUV system costs well over US$100M and is priced on value and scarcity.
context_what_they_do: We hold a complete monopoly on EUV lithography — there is no second supplier, and we control over 90% of the global lithography market. This rests on more than 2,000 EUV patents covering the technology, developed over 30 years of R&D at a cost no competitor could justify repeating. Our optics come from Zeiss exclusively, and we hold a stake in Zeiss SMT so that supply cannot be redirected to a rival; the light source, the optics and the precision mechanics are integrated such that no single component can be substituted. We are supported by a network of around 5,000 suppliers that took decades to assemble and is not replicable. Once a fab is built around our machines, the tooling, process recipes and process control are all calibrated to us, so the installed base cannot switch. Every leading-edge semiconductor in the world is produced on our equipment, and the leading-edge nodes cannot be manufactured without it.
undercut_on: Nothing that matters. Competitors have attempted EUV development and withdrawn — the engineering and capital requirements were prohibitive. We are not cheaper; we are the only option. The residual risk is geopolitical export controls and our customers' own capex cycles, neither of which is a competitor.
competes_with: Canon (DUV and nanoimprint — no EUV capability); Nikon (DUV only — withdrew from EUV development); Applied Materials / Lam Research (adjacent deposition and etch, not lithography); Chinese state-backed lithography efforts (SSMB and domestic EUV programmes)

category: Health supplements for women — joint, bone and mobility support, positioned around menopause and perimenopause.
price: Premium — materially above mass-market joint supplements.
context_what_they_do: We spent years in R&D developing a formulation that combines Traditional Chinese Medicine principles with modern nutritional science into a single proprietary blend. The specification is not published - we protect the formulation as a trade secret rather than a patent, because a patent would require us to disclose the exact composition and ratios and would expire, whereas a trade secret does not expire if it is not reverse-engineered. The ingredients must be extracted a particular way and combined in a specific sequence and ratio; getting the ratios wrong produces a materially different product, and that sequence is the part we do not disclose. We also developed the manufacturing process ourselves rather than using a contract manufacturer's off-the-shelf blend, which means the process is ours and not available to anyone else through a supplier. The name is trademarked. We do not believe the blend can be replicated by simply copying the ingredient list, because the extraction and sequencing are where the effect comes from and they are not visible in a finished capsule.
undercut_on: Price. Larger supplement brands sell generic joint products far cheaper, and they are on every pharmacy shelf where we are not. A customer who does not believe in the formulation just buys the cheapest glucosamine.

label_source_external: The 17-case corpus is 12/17 MARKET-ELASTIC, so the elasticity hypothesis could not fail there. This case supplies the opposite prediction: a duopoly whose market supply is INELASTIC (physical tooling + certification ceiling), where unmet demand must therefore accumulate as an order book. Hypothesis predicts HIGH headroom. Watsons/Guardian (F2) is the same duopoly structure with ELASTIC supply and predicts LOW. Two opposite predictions = a test that can fail.

category: Online retail and delivery in South Korea — everyday goods, groceries and fresh food, delivered to the home.
price: Competitive on everyday goods; membership fee for Wow.
context_what_they_do: Our advantage is not any single product or patent — it is a system that compounds. We built our own delivery network end to end instead of renting third-party couriers, which is what lets us deliver by 7am on orders placed after midnight. Because we own the whole route, delivery density is ours to improve: the more orders in a given area, the cheaper each drop becomes, and we convert that into lower prices and faster delivery, which brings more orders into the same area. That loop has been running for over a decade and is why we now serve the majority of Korean online shoppers. Our Wow membership makes the default choice automatic for tens of millions of people, so our volume advantage widens rather than narrows. A competitor would have to fund years of losses and rebuild the entire physical network before the loop even started turning — and by then the density advantage would be larger than when they began. We also run our own fresh-food and grocery operations on the same network, which no competitor has combined at this scale.
undercut_on: Nothing structurally. Early on we were the most expensive option to run and lost money for a decade doing it. Smaller players compete on price for specific categories but cannot match speed, and none can match the breadth of what we deliver next morning.
competes_with: Naver Shopping (marketplace and search-led commerce); SSG.com and E-Mart (Shinsegae's grocery and online arm); CJ Logistics (third-party delivery provider); Kurly / Market Kurly (fresh grocery, next-morning)
